name: Style Your Portfolio
description: Learn CSS by styling the personal portfolio page you built with HTML.

introduction.title: Style with CSS
introduction.description: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) is what makes websites look beautiful. It handles colors, fonts, layouts, and animations.

lessons.title: Colors & Typography
lessons.description: Bring your portfolio to life with colors and custom fonts.

challenges.title: Set the body font and background
challenges.description: Great portfolios start with clean, readable typography.

learn.heading: What is CSS?
paragraphs: CSS controls how HTML elements look. You write selectors (like `body` or `h1`) and declare style rules.
The `body` selector targets the whole page — setting fonts and background here affects everything unless overridden.

learn.heading: Further Reading
paragraphs: Read the MDN CSS reference for `font-family` and `background-color` to learn more.

textbook.title: MDN CSS reference
textbook.excerpt: MDN provides authoritative docs and examples for CSS properties.

questions.prompt: Which CSS selector would you use to set a page-wide font and background?
Which property sets the background color of the page?

challenges.title: Style the main heading
challenges.description: Make the portfolio owner's name stand out with a bold, dark color.

learn.heading: Headings and size
paragraphs: Heading styles come from selectors like `h1`. Use `font-size` and `color` to control appearance.

questions.prompt: What property sets the size of text in CSS?
Which unit is commonly used for responsive font sizing?

challenges.instructions: Add an h1 rule that sets color to #2c3e50 and font-size to 2rem.

challenges.title: Style the navigation links
challenges.description: Remove the default blue underlined links and give your nav a fresh look.

learn.heading: Styling links
paragraphs: Links use the `a` selector. `text-decoration: none` removes underlines; color changes the link colour.

questions.prompt: Which property removes the underline from links?
Which selector targets links inside a nav element?

challenges.instructions: Add a nav a rule: set color to #3498db, text-decoration to none, and margin-right to 12px.

lessons.title: Box Model & Spacing
lessons.description: Use padding, margin, and borders to give your portfolio room to breathe.

challenges.title: Pad each section
challenges.description: Sections feel cramped without spacing — padding fixes that.
challenges.instructions: Add a section rule with padding: 24px and margin-bottom: 20px to give each section breathing room.

challenges.title: Style the project card
challenges.description: A border and rounded corners turn a plain div into a polished card.
challenges.instructions: Add a .card rule with: border: 1px solid #ddd, border-radius: 8px, padding: 16px, and background-color: #fff.

challenges.title: Center the page content
challenges.description: A max-width with auto margins keeps your page readable on wide screens.
challenges.instructions: Update the body rule: add max-width: 800px, margin: 0 auto, and padding: 20px to center and frame the content.

lessons.title: Flexbox Layout
lessons.description: Use flexbox to build powerful, responsive layouts with just a few lines of CSS.

challenges.title: Flex the navigation
challenges.description: Flexbox arranges nav links into a clean horizontal row effortlessly.
challenges.instructions: Add a nav rule with display: flex and gap: 12px to lay your links out in a row with even spacing.

challenges.title: Flex the project cards
challenges.description: Use flexbox on the projects section so multiple cards sit side by side.
challenges.instructions: Add an #projects rule with display: flex, flex-wrap: wrap, and gap: 16px so cards flow into a responsive grid.

challenges.title: Make cards grow evenly
challenges.description: The flex shorthand lets each card claim its fair share of the available space.
challenges.instructions: Add a new .card rule with flex: 1 and min-width: 200px so cards expand evenly and wrap gracefully on narrow screens.
